Here is the issue:
Issue Title: Issues with writing file names

Description:
Hi, great tool!

I just starting trying it, and I'm running into some issues. 

Initially, I was encountering the same problem as detailed in this issue: https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/issues/167. Fortunately, I noticed you fixed this and after pulling the changes, that issue was resolved.

However, I'm now facing another issue related to file name generation. The program is formatting file names as '`filename`':
![image](https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/assets/25695071/6fe9db63-3b14-481d-8182-8c8ed5e9f75f)

At other (most) times, it's formatting them as '[filename]', which is resulting in file outputs like this:

![image](https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/assets/25695071/801f1da0-6968-4001-9bba-882d0db40c42)

I suspect this might have something to do with this commit: https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/commit/8180f0346c8a380637b72212432aa9abd5c04a9c#diff-945067bb601867dd64fd5ae92de9bf829da8545700835ac49744902ddec355fd

I'm using gpt-3.5-turbo since I don't have access to gpt-4 yet. Maybe the model is not as smart to understand this prompt?

Here are the possible buggy locations collected by someone else. Each location contains the actual code snippet and the intended behavior of the code for resolving the issue. Location #1: gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py None parse_chat 4 def parse_chat(chat): # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]: 5 # Get all ``` blocks and preceding filenames 6 regex = r"(\S+?)\n```\S+\n(.+?)```" 7 matches = re.finditer(regex, chat, re.DOTALL) 8 9 files = [] 10 for match in matches: 11 # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters and convert / to \ 12 path = re.sub(r'[<>"|?*]', "", match.group(1)) 13 14 # Get the code 15 code = match.group(2) 16 17 # Add the file to the list 18 files.append((path, code)) 19 20 # Get all the text before the first ``` block 21 readme = chat.split("```")[0] 22 files.append(("README.md", readme)) 23 24 # Return the files 25 return files This function should robustly parse file names from the chat output and sanitize them by removing extraneous formatting characters such as backticks (`) and square brackets ([]), in addition to the currently removed special characters. This will ensure that file names are clean and consistent regardless of GPT model output formatting differences, thus preventing malformed file names like '`filename`' or '[filename]'. The content extraction logic should remain unchanged to preserve file contents integrity. Location #2: gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py None to_files 28 def to_files(chat, workspace): 29 workspace["all_output.txt"] = chat 30 31 files = parse_chat(chat) 32 for file_name, file_content in files: 33 workspace[file_name] = file_content This function should continue to delegate file name and content extraction to `parse_chat` and map them correctly into the workspace. It may remain unchanged if `parse_chat` adequately fixes the filename formatting issue. If further adjustments are needed, they should ensure correctly formatted filenames are used as keys without extraneous characters. Note that you DO NOT NEED to modify every location; you should think what changes are necessary for resolving the issue, and only propose those modifications.

Write a patch for the issue, based on the relevant code context.
First explain the reasoning, and then write the actual patch.
When writing the patch, remember the following:
 - You do not have to modify every location provided - just make the necessary changes.
 - Pay attention to the addtional context as well - sometimes it might be better to fix there.

since the system will use this to locate the code to be modified.

Reasoning:
The root cause of the issue is that the filename in the chat output sometimes includes extraneous characters such as backticks (`) or square brackets ([]), and currently, the code only strips some special characters (like `< > " | ? *`) but does not handle these backticks or brackets. This results in malformed file names like "`filename`" or "[filename]". To fix this, the parsing function `parse_chat` should be enhanced to clean the filename by removing any leading/trailing backticks and square brackets in addition to existing sanitization.

No other changes are necessary, since `to_files` delegates correctly to `parse_chat`.

Patch:

```
<file>gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py</file>
<original>4 def parse_chat(chat):  # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
5     # Get all ``` blocks and preceding filenames
6     regex = r"(\S+?)\n```\S+\n(.+?)```"
7     matches = re.finditer(regex, chat, re.DOTALL)
8 
9     files = []
10     for match in matches:
11         # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters and convert / to \
12         path = re.sub(r'[<>"|?*]', "", match.group(1))
13 
14         # Get the code
15         code = match.group(2)
16 
17         # Add the file to the list
18         files.append((path, code))
19 
20     # Get all the text before the first ``` block
21     readme = chat.split("```")[0]
22     files.append(("README.md", readme))
23 
24     # Return the files
25     return files
</original>
<patched>4 def parse_chat(chat):  # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
5     # Get all ``` blocks and preceding filenames
6     regex = r"(\S+?)\n```\S+\n(.+?)```"
7     matches = re.finditer(regex, chat, re.DOTALL)

9     files = []
10     for match in matches:
11         # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters and convert / to \
12         path = re.sub(r'[<>"|?*]', "", match.group(1))
13         # Also strip surrounding backticks and square brackets from filename
14         path = path.strip("`[]")
15

17         code = match.group(2)
18

20         files.append((path, code))
21
